text.p: These are the leading stories in the Moroccan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hassan welcomes Italian President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro who is on a three-day visit to Morocco.
- Interior Minister Driss Basri tells Hague conference on management of public affairs in the Euro-Mediterranean region that "globalisation imposes major adjustments".
- Italian President Scalfaro and King Hassan to inaugurate Morocco's biggest dam, Al Wahda.
- Cuts on investment loans and treasury bond rates not enough to boost investments deterred by threat of drought and fear of competition ahead of free trade zone with EU.
- Casablanca appeal court confirms verdict on customs officers jailed on smuggling charges.
- James Baker, the United Nations special envoy in Western Sahara, has mission to break deadlock over referendum.
- U.N. envoy James Baker to visit Western Sahara next month.
- Inauguration of Al Wahda dam will bring irrigated land to one million hectares (2.5 million acres).
- Balance of payments showed surplus of 788 million dirhams ($84.7 million) during first half of 1996 against deficit in same period in 1995.
- Al-Qods committee is preparing counter offensive to Israeli decision to establish settlements in East Jerusalem.
